items.title: Bill Huntington and Charlie Suhor Interview, 1992-04-06
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well, we used to play and Herb Tasson used to come and jam with us at the, at the Premiers Fountain Lounge Club.

ctx.x: Ironic, sort of a sardonic singing style, you know. But our involvement during that time is very close, because we played a lot together. And that also helped my development. You know, just playing and being around a person of my own age who was into music. Then I met Charlie through Buddy, met Al Herman, who was a great trombonist. Let's see, who else was in that peer group kind of?

Well, we used to play and Herb Tasson used to come and jam with us at the, at the Premiers Fountain Lounge Club. And a lot of people used to hang around there, because, you know, they liked, we were a rhythm section, and a pretty damn good one. So guys used to come and jam with us, but as far, oh yeah, well. Charlie Miller.

Charlie Miller, who's now living back in New Orleans, is a very, really excellent jazz trumpet player, classical trumpet player as well. And Jimmy Asenheimer, who was a really excellent clarinetist, played with the symphony, and was involved in, Buddy used to have an interesting term for the kind of music we were all kind of getting involved in. We were all getting interested in modern classical music as well. And most of us were studying composition. I had studied for a while with John Butler, who was kind of a…
